claims.text: Equiatomic HfMoTaTiZr has a density greater than 12 g/cm³.
Conventional equiatomic HfMoTaTiZr is strong but severely brittle at room temperature because of single-phase BCC behavior or brittle intermetallic formation.
A composition in Hf-Mo-Ta-Ti-Zr can be tuned to undergo a pseudo-binary eutectic reaction producing B2-ordered and disordered BCC phases.
SLM with high energy input and cooling rate produces rapid solidification.
Rapid solidification will reduce the target alloy's grain size below 15 μm and dendrite arm spacing below 7 μm.
A post-SLM heat treatment can optimize B2/BCC lamellar spacing and phase fraction in Hf-Mo-Ta-Ti-Zr.
The processed Hf-Mo-Ta-Ti-Zr alloy will contain a fine, regular, alternating B2/BCC lamellar microstructure.
Hard B2 regions pin dislocations moving through the soft disordered BCC matrix, producing work hardening and delaying fracture.
Rapid-solidification grain refinement enhances alloy strength.
A Pugh ratio above 1.75 and positive Cauchy pressure indicate intrinsic ductility.
The proposed alloy will have room-temperature yield strength above 1000 MPa.
The proposed alloy will have room-temperature tensile elongation above 10%.
The proposed alloy will be approximately 10–15% less dense than equiatomic HfMoTaTiZr.
Increasing the volume fraction of a Ti/Zr-rich BCC phase mitigates the density contribution of Hf and Ta.
The proposed alloy will maintain high-temperature stability.
The strength-ductility mechanism requires the composition to remain within a pseudo-binary eutectic region.
Formation of brittle TCP phases will cause the proposed alloy's ductility to fail.
Excessive B2 ordering causes brittleness, whereas insufficient B2 ordering causes low strength.
Powder-bed laser processing can cause cracking through process-induced internal stress acting in an alloy with insufficient low-temperature ductility.
Build-platform preheating can mitigate process-induced cracking.

contradictions.description: The initial state is described simultaneously as an elemental powder mixture and as a coarse-grained as-cast state; these are distinct material states.
